item.text: {"search_note":"I did not find direct evidence that Srettha used state power to suppress auditors, prosecutors, or whistleblowers specifically. I also did not find direct evidence of concealed campaign-finance manipulation or a documented effort to hide official decisions through records destruction or formal secrecy. The strongest evidence is indirect: press intimidation, avoidance of human-rights scrutiny, and the ethics case around Pichit Chuenban.","evidence":[{"title":"Srettha and his wife worth B1bn","publisher":"Bangkok Post","date":"June 17, 2024","url":"https://www.bangkokpost.com/thailand/politics/2812379/declaration","summary":"Srettha and his wife publicly declared substantial assets to the National Anti-Corruption Commission. This is weak but real positive evidence that he tolerated some external scrutiny of personal finances.","question_ids":["7B.7","7B.6"]},{"title":"Thailand | Reuters Institute for the Study of Journalism","publisher":"Reuters Institute for the Study of Journalism","date":"June 17, 2024","url":"https://reutersinstitute.politics.ox.ac.uk/digital-news-report/2024/thailand","summary":"The report says Thai media could still criticize government policy and report corruption, and mainstream outlets continued verification work.
